ElectricWealthAIDE / AIDE Lab / Bootcamp Days 4-5

From brownfield exercises to a delivered feature

Prepare your workspace, install AIDE, initialize, analyze, reverse engineer and build the KB. Adopt matched checkpoints at the instructor's handoffs, then define, plan, implement and review a feature on your own branches.

Everyone attempts the guided bootstrap exercises. The instructor sets segment boundaries; checkpoints standardize the foundation without declaring unfinished work passed. Feature-delivery lessons are instructions, not completed feature evidence.

Single-file review copy: all lessons, 17 native screenshots and original sample/transcript downloads are embedded. Dotted references point to the historical workspace, not bundled files. External web links are optional.

Preparation / Start here

Prepare the local workspace

Objective: Create your personal branches and a four-root workspace from the instructor's starter revisions. Install AIDE in the following, separate lesson.

Course setup documentation

Do

  • Review the workspace setup plan.
  • Approve it only when the starter revisions and your own branch names are clear.

Ready to continue when

  • The sibling repositories, personal branches and starter revisions are confirmed. AIDE installation follows in its own lesson.
Review before setup

Review the workspace plan before approving changes. Send the two prompts below one at a time. AIDE installation is the next, separate lesson.

1. Chat with your AI agent

Instructor-authored sample prompts. Start with the first one; review the plan before approving.

1. Ask the agent to check access and propose a plan

Replace <repo-parent> with your local course folder. Ask the instructor for the starter revisions, not the completed RE/KB checkpoints.

Help me prepare this project for an AI-led AIDE course in VS Code.

Project repositories:
- Workspace: https://dev.azure.com/IntelliwareDev/AI_Knowledge_Repo/_git/course-project-workspace
- Knowledge base: https://dev.azure.com/IntelliwareDev/AI_Knowledge_Repo/_git/course-knowledge-base
- Specifications: https://dev.azure.com/IntelliwareDev/AI_Knowledge_Repo/_git/course-specifications-repo
- Application: https://dev.azure.com/IntelliwareDev/AI_Knowledge_Repo/_git/ElectricWealthAIDE

The four project repositories should be sibling folders under <repo-parent>.
The end result should be a VS Code multi-root workspace containing the four project roots.
Use the instructor's starter revisions for the guided bootstrap exercises. Pause if a starter revision is missing; do not substitute a completed checkpoint or latest main.
Include creation of my own course branch in each project repository before any project-file changes.

First confirm read access to all four project repositories using authenticated Git and outline the clone, branch and workspace steps.
Do not clone, install AIDE, create workspace files, or change branches yet.
If access is blocked, tell me what is needed without asking me to paste passwords or tokens into chat.
Wait for my approval of the plan.
2. Approve the reviewed plan

Only send this after reviewing the plan. Replace <your-course-branch> with your own name/branch; the reviewed plan must identify all starter revisions.

I approve the setup plan we just reviewed.
Please clone or reuse the four project repositories as siblings using the reviewed baseline revisions.
Use the instructor-approved starter revisions in the plan. Do not adopt the completed RE or KB checkpoints yet.
Create <your-course-branch> as my own course branch in each project repository before changing project files. If it already exists, verify it before reuse. Leave main and other participants' branches unchanged.
Once those branches are confirmed, create/open aide-course.code-workspace with the four project roots.
Preserve existing clones and working changes. Ask before overwriting anything or resolving a conflicting existing layout.
If authentication or a manual installation step is required, pause and guide me through it.
Confirm the final folder layout, workspace roots, starter revisions and personal branch status.
Stop there. Do not install AIDE or run /start-project yet. AIDE installation is the next dedicated lesson.

2. What good preparation looks like

Expected results, not captured agent output.

What to look for in the proposed plan

  • Read access confirmed for the four project repositories.
  • Four sibling workspace roots, using instructor-approved starter revisions.
  • Your approval before cloning or branch creation.

Ready to continue when

  • The four folders exist and appear in VS Code Explorer.
  • Your own course branch exists in each project repository; existing work is preserved and main is unchanged.
  • Starter revisions are confirmed. Completed checkpoints have not replaced the exercises.

Continue to Install AIDE in the prepared workspace. Installation and skill discovery are checked there.

VS Code with GitHub Copilot in agent mode is the demonstrated route. IntelliJ/Copilot is a deferred pilot, not a validated alternative in this guide. Experienced IntelliJ users should confirm sibling-repository access and skill discovery with the facilitator before relying on it; a .code-workspace file is not an IntelliJ setup.

These are expected outcomes, not historical agent responses.

is this a multiroot repo workspace?

2. Sample output

The selected recorded result and next-skill handoff, where present. This formatted text is not an agent-chat screenshot or a new execution.

Recorded assistant - T0163

Yes—the workspace is configured as a VS Code multi-root workspace. aide-course.code-workspace defines four roots:

  • Project workspace
  • Knowledge base
  • Specifications
  • ElectricWealthAIDE source

These are separate Git repositories. Within the source repository, the mobile app, mock API and contracts form a monorepo.

So: a multi-root, multi-repository workspace containing one application monorepo. To use that layout in VS Code, open the workspace file rather than just a single folder.

Lesson 1 of 17 / Required

Install AIDE in the prepared workspace

Objective: Install the pinned framework only after the multi-root workspace is ready, then verify skill discovery.

Do

  • Confirm the four workspace roots and your personal branches from preparation.
  • Ask the agent to read the R2.6.0 installation instructions from the framework source repository and propose the installation.
  • Approve the reviewed plan, then verify the install provenance and skills in a fresh VS Code Copilot agent chat.

Ready to continue when

  • AIDE is installed under course-project-workspace\AIDE, not in the application or KB.
  • Workspace-root skill discovery shims and orientation are present; the recorded release resolves to d61c5eb87d407b5d18435e5709fac6d50e699c31.
  • A fresh agent chat can discover /start-project. An unavailable skill is a blocker, not a reason to invent its behavior.

Prompt input

Authored course guidance. Replace placeholders, send one prompt at a time, and wait for the preceding review or decision.

Read the pinned installation process

The four-root workspace is ready. Plan AIDE installation in the course-project-workspace root.

AIDE_REF=R2.6.0
AIDE_TARGET_DIR=./AIDE

If reading requires a temporary clone, ask me first. Follow the release's documented Git fetch and installation process. Explain prerequisites and how existing installs or hand-authored files will be preserved.
Do not install, overwrite or update anything yet. Wait for my approval.

Use my existing personal course branches. Ask before creating/switching branches, committing, pushing, opening a PR or merging. Leave main and other participants' work unchanged.

Approve only after reviewing the plan

I approve the installation plan we just reviewed.
Install AIDE from the specified source at R2.6.0 under course-project-workspace\AIDE by following that release's INSTRUCTIONS.md.
Use authenticated Git preflight and the documented Git clone process; stop on authentication/network errors. Never ask me to paste passwords or tokens.
Preserve existing work and ask before overwriting an existing install; this is not blanket update permission.
Verify install provenance, mandatory framework folders, workspace-root discovery shims and orientation. Guide me to open a fresh VS Code Copilot agent chat and confirm /start-project appears.
Stop before invoking /start-project. We will run it in the next lesson.

Use my existing personal course branches. Ask before creating/switching branches, committing, pushing, opening a PR or merging. Leave main and other participants' work unchanged.

Lesson 4 of 17 / Required

Reverse engineer and review the application

Objective: Attempt source-derived documentation and understand its review before adopting the completed RE checkpoint.

Do

  • Invoke the mobile RE skill, then document the supporting API/contracts with the API skill.
  • Confirm source-local internal Part A and sibling-KB consumer/OpenAPI Part B paths; inspect persisted output.
  • Review the output and its conditions. At the instructor's segment boundary, preserve your actual progress and proceed to the checkpoint handoff without labeling an incomplete review passed.

Ready to continue when

  • You have attempted extraction and can locate Part A, Part B and an API specification.
  • You understand the review decisions and any unfinished work or blockers.
  • Existing deep-link/biometric limitations and the distinction between nominal contracts and actual mock responses remain explicit.

Adopt the completed RE checkpoint

Objective: Preserve your attempt, then use the matched reviewed documentation baseline for the KB exercise.

Do

  • At the instructor's handoff, save your exercise work with your approval; preserve any unfinished statuses.
  • Review the application and KB RE-only branch links below. Confirm instructor-approved revisions and provenance before adopting them.
  • Fetch both refs and create new participant-owned branches from them. Keep workspace/specifications configuration and verify all sibling pointers.

Ready to continue when

  • Your original exercise branch and work remain recoverable.
  • The application and KB are on your own branches derived from the matched RE-only checkpoint.
  • Part A is in the application; Part B/OpenAPI is in the KB. The RE-only KB has no generated component catalog or graph.

Recorded assistant - T0061

Repository analysis: ElectricWealthAIDE

Classification: TypeScript/pnpm monorepo containing a mobile application, a mock HTTP API, and a shared contract library.

The implementation is mobile-first—not a browser-based portal. The ui registration in project.toml was treated as a hint, not changed.

Components

Component Classification Evidence Documentation approach
mobile Mobile application Expo, React Native, iOS/Android configuration, navigation and wealth-management screens reverse-engineer-mobile-app
server API application Express routers for authentication, registration, wealth, market, advisor, profile and related features reverse-engineer-api
contract Internal shared contract library Exported Zod schemas and TypeScript types consumed by both applications Document alongside the API, then reference from mobile docs

The contract package is not a standalone UI/mobile framework or general backend framework; a separate framework RE pass would overstate its scope.

Stack and versions

From manifests and the lockfile, not runtime verification:

  • TypeScript 5.9.3
  • Expo 52.0.49, React Native 0.76.6, React 18.3.1
  • Express 4.22.2
  • Zod 3.25.76
  • Vitest 2.1.9, with Supertest for API tests

Workspace packages declare version 0.1.0; the Expo configuration separately declares app version 1.0.0.

Important boundaries

  • The server is explicitly a mock backend. Its database implementation uses seeded in-memory collections—not a persistent database. No separate database RE pass is warranted.
  • Mobile UI components are internal application code, not an independently packaged component library.
  • The co-located API tests belong in API testing documentation—not a dedicated test-suite RE pass.

Existing documentation

No README, documentation tree, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or TSDoc/JSDoc blocks were found in the scanned application sources. The RE passes will establish the initial documentation baseline.

Recommended order

  1. reverse-engineer-api — document the server and shared contracts first.
  2. reverse-engineer-mobile-app — document mobile workflows and their API dependencies.
  3. build-knowledge-base — aggregate the outputs into the configured knowledge base.

Each extraction must complete its close-out gate—automated verification or package review—before KB ingestion.

Run /reverse-engineer-api, targeting server and including contract in scope.

# Readiness Verdict - ElectricWealthAIDE Mobile Primary

**CONDITIONAL**, explicitly accepted on 2026-10-06.
The nine-step combined review is complete. Conditional KB ingestion is
permitted; starting it still requires the user's separate go-ahead.

## Outstanding findings - required handoff conditions

| Scoped finding | Severity | Accepted condition / one-line summary |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile [adversarial-findings.md](adversarial-findings.md), ADV-001 | high | Carry unassigned maintainer/consumer responsibilities until human-confirmed. |
| API [adversarial-findings.md](../../api-internal/review/adversarial-findings.md), ADV-001 | high | The same shared ownership gap must also accompany the supporting API baseline; not a second independent risk. |
| Mobile [adversarial-findings.md](adversarial-findings.md), ADV-002 | medium | Qualify biometric capability summaries with known integration impediments; no verified end-to-end claim. |
| Mobile [edge-case-findings.md](edge-case-findings.md), ADV-001 | high | Carry the reproduced duplicate `accounts/new` parser rejection; no working-link claim without a separately authorized repair and validation. |

There are four scoped finding records and three distinct combined issues.
The API [edge-case-findings.md](../../api-internal/review/edge-case-findings.md)
is the validated empty case, not another finding.

## Other accepted conditions

- Preserve all **23 mobile and 8 API UNVERIFIED marker lines**. They are
  unresolved source-external/rationale/device facts, not cleared tests.
- Preserve coarse-citation and semantic-grounding limits. Attribution-unit
  counts are not factual-error rates or correctness percentages.
- Do not claim normal workspace build/type-check, existing unit-suite,
  exhaustive error-path, emulator/device or production-readiness success.
- Preserve observed mock behavior and nominal-versus-actual contract
  differences. Do not silently promote demo controls into production features.

## Handoff boundary

The KB builder must load both readiness records with the consumer trees
and OpenAPI, carrying conditions into applicable component metadata or
explicit open-fact records. It must not ingest Part B alone as an
unqualified working-system attestation.

Baseline: source `4637a21bb776310fc113445e2e2509083a1eaf74`, package 0.1.0;
Expo app label 1.0.0 is separate. Source and manifests are unchanged.
No source repair, commit, push or KB construction occurred.

Details: [review-re-readiness.md](review-re-readiness.md).
First ingestion, once authorized, uses `build-knowledge-base`.

# ElectricWealthAIDE - Solution Overview

## 1. Mission

ElectricWealthAIDE is an internal sample wealth application used for the
AIDE bootcamp. It provides an existing base application that participants
use to add a new feature and gain hands-on experience delivering that feature
with AIDE. Once requirements are in place, participants design the solution,
plan implementation and implement the feature. The prepared knowledge base
is a backup if the KB-building portion exceeds the training time allocated to it.

## 2. Value Proposition

- Give participants hands-on experience delivering a new feature with AIDE
  in an existing application.
- Provide a shared existing application as the starting point for feature
  work, with a prepared KB fallback when building the KB takes longer than
  the training allocation permits.

These are human-confirmed learning outcomes, not claims of measured course
effectiveness or production business value. Targets and baselines belong in
the goals/KPIs leaf.

## 3. Out of Scope

- Production release of this bootcamp base application.
- Live financial operations or live financial-system integrations.
- Use of real client financial data.

The application demonstrates wealth-management interfaces; this mission
does not authorize real banking, trading, financial advice or deployment.

## 4. Classification

Classification is grounded in the reviewed code baseline and
[architecture index](../../ARCHITECTURE.md), not inferred from the course
roles or the number of workspace folders.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project type(s) | Mobile application, supporting mock HTTP API and internal shared contracts |
| Primary languages | TypeScript, including TSX for React Native presentation |
| Architecture pattern | Mobile-first hybrid: Expo/React Native app, modular Express mock process, internal Zod contracts |
| Repo count | One indexed application source monorepo: electricwealth-aide |
| Workspace layout | Four roots: project workspace, knowledge base, specifications and application source; these are not four application services |
| Registered source role | ui (broad registry role); observed primary application is mobile, not a browser app |

The indexed source surfaces are [mobile-runtime](../../components/electricwealth-aide/mobile-runtime.md),
[api-runtime](../../components/electricwealth-aide/api-runtime.md) and
[shared-contracts](../../components/electricwealth-aide/shared-contracts.md).
The application uses mock server fixtures, not a persistent server database
or an attested production financial platform.

Capture provenance identifies Instructor as the person confirming these
answers. It does not assign maintainership, decision authority, RACI or
on-call responsibility.

Readiness remains **CONDITIONAL**. The
[accepted conditions](../../_meta/conditions.md) retain unresolved shared-repository approval authority,
biometric integration impediments, the reproduced deep-link parser conflict,
operational/device unknowns and bounded evidence. Capturing this mission does
not repair those issues or attest normal build/test, native journeys or release.

## 6. Links Forward

- [Personas and use cases](10-personas-and-use-cases.md).
- [Goals and KPIs](20-goals-and-kpis.md).
- [Constraints and compliance](30-constraints-and-compliance.md).
- [External integrations](40-external-integrations.md).
- [Ownership and RACI](50-ownership-and-raci.md).
- [Architecture capability index](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-capability-index).

There is no multi-repository application summary: the project registers one
application source repo, despite having four roots in its development workspace.

# ElectricWealthAIDE - Personas and Use Cases

## 1. Persona Catalog

| Label | Segment | Primary Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Bootcamp participant | Cross-functional delivery participants, including developers, analysts, QA and architects, across technical and non-technical learning contexts | Practice delivering a feature with AIDE in an existing application, contributing according to role |

Instructor confirmed participants as the complete persona set for this leaf.
An operator/support persona was explicitly proposed and excluded. Instructor
is capture provenance, not an automatically included persona or an assigned
maintainer. Operational accountability is a separate ownership/RACI topic.

The sample application's financial/staff profiles are simulated application
context, not confirmed production customers or additional course personas.

## 2. Persona Detail

### Bootcamp Participant

**Sketch:** Participants come from cross-functional delivery and mixed
technical/non-technical backgrounds. They use a shared existing wealth
application to understand a baseline and available requirements, design the
solution, plan implementation, contribute to implementation/testing according
to their role, and review the result.
The exercise is not limited to everyone writing application code.

**Jobs-to-be-done:**

| When (situation) | I want (motivation) | So I can (outcome) | Frequency | Criticality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starting an assigned feature exercise | Understand the existing app and its mobile/API/contracts boundaries | Ground the exercise in the actual baseline | Once per assigned feature exercise | Failure can block the exercise or learning outcome |
| Requirements for the assigned change are in place | Design the solution and plan implementation with AIDE | Make the technical approach and delivery work clear before implementation | Once per assigned feature exercise | Failure can block the exercise or learning outcome |
| Carrying out the plan | Contribute to implementation and testing according to my role | Participate in delivering the feature rather than only observing the method | Once per assigned feature exercise | Failure can block the exercise or learning outcome |
| Reviewing the exercise result | Review the delivered feature and its supporting work | Understand the result of the AIDE delivery journey | Once per assigned feature exercise | Failure can block the exercise or learning outcome |

These consequences concern the exercise and learning. They do not imply
customer impact, live financial operations or production availability loss.
No individual skill level, accessibility need, assessment rubric or personal
pain point has been inferred from the role labels.

## 3. Jobs-to-Component Map

| Persona | Job statement | Component IDs |
|---|---|---|
| Bootcamp participant | Understand the existing application baseline and its boundaries | [mobile-runtime](../../components/electricwealth-aide/mobile-runtime.md), [mobile-navigation](../../components/electricwealth-aide/mobile-navigation.md), [api-runtime](../../components/electricwealth-aide/api-runtime.md), [shared-contracts](../../components/electricwealth-aide/shared-contracts.md) |
| Bootcamp participant | Design the solution and plan implementation after requirements are in place | No universal application runtime component; this is course/delivery work |
| Bootcamp participant | Contribute to feature implementation and testing according to role | Feature-specific selection pending the assigned exercise scope |
| Bootcamp participant | Review the exercise result | Feature-specific selection pending the assigned exercise scope |

TODO(catalog): Once an exercise feature is selected, link its implementation
and review jobs to existing in-scope components through the
[capability index](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-capability-index). This is deferred
feature scoping, not a claim that a course workflow is an uncatalogued
application runtime feature. No new component ID or feature ID is invented.

Baseline component links describe where to investigate, not successful native
journeys. In particular, the navigation parser conflict and other
[accepted conditions](../../_meta/conditions.md) remain explicit. This persona
catalog does not repair source defects. The
[ownership capture](50-ownership-and-raci.md) separately confirms that each
participant controls every step and approval of their assigned feature,
with optional consultation and no mandatory informed audience.

The [overview](00-overview.md) records the prepared KB's fallback role when
the KB-building training segment overruns. The
[goals](20-goals-and-kpis.md) record the confirmed target of one reviewed
feature per participant and the facilitators' result/fallback decision role.
That role does not add an instructor persona to this participant-only catalog
or create an extra feature approval gate. Shared-source maintainership is
separately assigned to facilitators in the ownership capture.

# ElectricWealthAIDE - Goals and KPIs

## 1. Outcomes

- Hands-on delivery with AIDE: each participant delivers one reviewed
  feature by the end of its delivery exercise. This is not merely watching
  an implementation demonstration.
- A usable shared starting point and fallback: a prepared KB is available
  when the training's KB-building portion exceeds its allocated time,
  allowing participants to continue the delivery workflow.

Requirements must be in place before participants design the solution,
plan implementation and implement the feature. The [ownership capture](50-ownership-and-raci.md) assigns each participant
control of every step and approval of their assigned feature; requirements
authorship was not separately specified.

## 2. KPIs

| Name | Type | Definition | Baseline | Target | Horizon | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reviewed feature delivery | north-star | Count of delivered features per participant with review confirmed by the instructor/facilitators | TODO(baseline): participant delivery counts have not been measured <!-- Responsible: Instructor or bootcamp facilitators; collect the starting count and review record for each participant. --> | One reviewed feature per participant | End of the assigned delivery exercise | Instructor or bootcamp facilitators |
| Design and planning before implementation | leading | For each assigned feature, completion of a solution design and an implementation plan after requirements are available and before implementation begins | TODO(baseline): participant design/planning completion has not been measured <!-- Responsible: Instructor or bootcamp facilitators; record the two deliverables and their ordering for each assigned feature. --> | Both preparatory deliverables completed before implementation | During the assigned exercise, before coding/implementation | Instructor or bootcamp facilitators |
| Prepared KB fallback availability | leading | Presence of a prepared, source-grounded KB that facilitators can supply when the KB-building training segment overruns | One local code-grounded baseline exists and has passed the static coverage sweep; participant access/distribution is not confirmed | One prepared fallback KB available when required | When the KB-building segment exceeds its allocated training time | Instructor or bootcamp facilitators |
| Training-only financial-data boundary | guardrail | Count of production releases, live financial operations/integrations or uses of real client financial data in the bootcamp exercise | TODO(baseline): no course-wide audit or participant-data provenance measurement has been recorded <!-- Responsible: Instructor or bootcamp facilitators; verify exercise data, integration configuration and release behavior before use. --> | Zero occurrences in all three excluded categories | Throughout the bootcamp exercise | Instructor or bootcamp facilitators |

No fixed calendar deadline, exact KB-segment allocation, participant count,
tracking platform or numeric participant baseline has been supplied. The
course-relative horizons above were explicitly confirmed. KPI ownership is
confirmed for course result review and fallback decisions, not an additional
feature approval gate. Participants approve their own assigned feature work.
Source maintenance is separately assigned to facilitators in the
[ownership capture](50-ownership-and-raci.md); deployment and on-call
responsibility are not inferred from these KPI roles.

Portable construction evidence is the
[initial build report](../../_meta/build-report.md): 310/310 extracted artifacts
attributed across 24 components, with zero orphans under that build's scope.
The subsequent independent baseline sweep on 2026-10-06 reported 345/345 source
interfaces mapped, 24 source-backed components and zero orphans or stales.
The two counts use different enumeration scopes and are not interchangeable.
The independent report is local and Git-ignored, so its machine evidence is
not distributed in a fresh clone; its dated result is recorded here without
an unavailable report link. These checks establish static coverage, not
participant distribution, source defect repair, normal builds/tests or a
successful native journey. Human context has since been captured separately.

## 3. Trade-offs

- Facilitators may use the prepared KB when the KB-building portion overruns
  rather than allowing that portion to consume the remaining delivery exercise.
- The fallback supports the subsequent requirements/design/planning/implementation
  journey; it is not evidence that every participant completed KB construction.
- Completing a learning exercise does not justify a production release,
  live financial operation/integration or real-client-data use.
- A metric is not marked achieved merely because a component or dependency exists.
  Participant results and review evidence must be recorded separately.
- Known [baseline conditions](../../_meta/conditions.md) remain visible;
  coverage and these target definitions do not waive them.

## 4. Cross-references

| KPI | Linked components | Linked constraints |
|---|---|---|
| Reviewed feature delivery | Select the assigned feature's components through the [capability index](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-capability-index); no feature ID/component set is invented | [Participant journey](10-personas-and-use-cases.md), [training-only scope](00-overview.md#3-out-of-scope) |
| Design and planning before implementation | This is delivery work, not an application runtime component or telemetry system | Requirements precede design; design/planning precede implementation |
| Prepared KB fallback availability | [Architecture/catalog](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and [graph](../../graph.json), not a new course-monitoring application component | Training time allocation amount remains unconfirmed; instructor/facilitators decide when the fallback is needed |
| Training-only financial-data boundary | Feature-dependent checks; no component claims automated course compliance measurement | [Confirmed exclusions](00-overview.md#3-out-of-scope) and [constraints/compliance](30-constraints-and-compliance.md) |

The empty related_components array is intentional: these are course-level
measures, not application metrics emitted by one runtime module.

from the sample's wealth-management interfaces.

| Training-only financial-data boundary | Project-wide: no production release, live financial operations/integrations or real client financial data | Instructor-confirmed mission and guardrail KPI, 2026-10-06 | Active | Instructor or bootcamp facilitators for course guardrail confirmation | Manual review of exercise data, integration configuration and release behavior | [Training-only financial-data boundary](20-goals-and-kpis.md#2-kpis) |

# ElectricWealthAIDE - Ownership and RACI

Instructor confirmed these assignments on 2026-10-06. Capture provenance alone
does not assign ownership; the explicit answers below do. Facilitators form
one role/team in this document, including the Instructor.

R = Responsible (executes work), A = Accountable (final approval),
C = Consulted, I = Informed. A populated A cell names one role/team.
An unassigned A is an unresolved decision, not a second accountable team.

## 1. Repo Ownership

| Repo | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [electricwealth-aide](../../../ElectricWealthAIDE) - shared source-repository maintenance | Instructor/bootcamp facilitators | Unassigned: shared-repository final approval authority was explicitly left open | Optional; no mandatory role specified | No mandatory audience specified |

Only one application repo is registered in the
[repository map](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#2-repository-map). The workspace,
specifications and KB repos are separate work-product roots, not additional
application repos. Their maintainership was not assigned by this answer.

The shared-source maintenance role does not create a facilitator approval
gate for each participant's exercise.

### Assigned Feature RACI

| Work scope | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Every step and approval of a participant's own assigned feature | Assigned participant | Assigned participant | Optional, at participant discretion | No mandatory audience specified |

Participant authority applies to their assigned feature, not to final
shared-repository governance. No feature ID, participant name or scope has
been invented. The [delivery sequence and training boundaries](30-constraints-and-compliance.md)
still apply. Requirements availability remains the prerequisite to design;
requirements authorship was not separately specified.

The facilitators' [course KPI confirmation and KB-fallback decisions](20-goals-and-kpis.md)
remain separate from participant approval. Confirming the learning result
does not turn the facilitator into the feature's final approver.

## 2. Capability Ownership (Overrides)

No capability-specific ownership exceptions were specified - confirmed by
Instructor on 2026-10-06. Within each participant's assigned feature, all
selected capabilities follow that participant's feature RACI, including
authentication/security-related changes. Outside assigned feature work, the
shared-source row applies, with final shared-repository authority unresolved.

There are no differing capability rows to add to the
[capability index](../../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-capability-index).
This is not permission to exceed the training-only scope.

## 3. On-call Rotations

| Rotation | Scope | Tier 1 team | Tier 2 escalation | Tier 3 escalation | Paging tool | Handover cadence | Comms channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No formal rotation - confirmed by Instructor on 2026-10-06 | Training sample | None specified | No formal escalation structure | No formal escalation structure | None specified | Not applicable | None specified |

Source maintenance and course facilitation do not imply 24/7 support,
incident-response commitments or an informal escalation path not supplied
by the user.

## 4. Decision-Rights Matrix

| Decision class | Authority | Consultation required |
|---|---|---|
| Architecture within an assigned feature | Assigned participant | Optional; no mandatory consultation role specified |
| Security within an assigned feature | Assigned participant | Optional; no mandatory consultation role specified |
| Product decisions within an assigned feature | Assigned participant | Optional; no mandatory consultation role specified |
| Approval of every assigned-feature delivery step | Assigned participant | Optional; facilitator course-result confirmation is not an additional feature approval gate |
| Shared-repository final decisions, including architecture/security/product decisions beyond an assigned feature | Unassigned | No mandatory role specified |
| Course-result confirmation and prepared KB fallback use | Instructor/bootcamp facilitators | No mandatory consultation role specified |
| Hiring/team structure | Unspecified; no authority captured for this training exercise | No requirement captured |

These are training decision rights, not production security or release
authorization. No minimum review rubric or mandatory consultation process
was supplied.

## 5. Remaining Ownership Limits

- Shared-source maintainers are now human-confirmed as Instructor/bootcamp
  facilitators; bootcamp participants are the confirmed course consumers.
- Shared-repository final approval authority remains explicitly unassigned.
- KB/specification/workspace maintainership and a participant-specific feature
  assignment remain uncaptured.
- The original `ownership-unassigned` review condition is **partially
  addressed, not closed**. See [accepted conditions](../../_meta/conditions.md);
  original source-review records remain historical evidence.
- Other biometric, deep-link, operational/device and validation limits are
  unaffected. No application source repairs were made.

# Glossary

<!-- solution-context delta - captured on 2026-10-06 by Instructor -->

The following course terms were explicitly approved during solution-context
capture; they supplement, rather than replace, the existing source references.

- **Bootcamp participant** - A learner delivering an assigned feature with AIDE in the existing sample application.
- **Assigned feature** - The participant-controlled exercise change for which that participant owns every step and approval.
- **Reviewed feature** - A delivered feature with review recorded for the course outcome, not an additional facilitator approval gate.
- **Prepared KB fallback** - The source-grounded backup knowledge base facilitators can supply when the KB-building training segment exceeds its allocated time.
- **Design and planning before implementation** - The delivery order in which requirements are available first, then a solution design and implementation plan are completed before coding.
